### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4f7aa88a1cd376afbcfcfb51e80c2cce4300586a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `49a44732699b45382f4f66b01b9fa14ce600368d` — the merge of head `2c464d444b8b4d97ead6992e19071d78bcc8cee2` into base `4f7aa88a1cd376afbcfcfb51e80c2cce4300586a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 49a44732699b45382f4f66b01b9fa14ce600368d && git checkout 49a44732699b45382f4f66b01b9fa14ce600368d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4f7aa88a1cd376afbcfcfb51e80c2cce4300586a 2c464d444b8b4d97ead6992e19071d78bcc8cee2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4f7aa88a1cd376afbcfcfb51e80c2cce4300586a && git merge --no-ff 2c464d444b8b4d97ead6992e19071d78bcc8cee2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4f7aa88a1cd376afbcfcfb51e80c2cce4300586a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4f7aa88a1cd376afbcfcfb51e80c2cce4300586a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c5e44f02f492b8be18709f906e1678a5697af79b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts + packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.test.ts, ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/__tests__/toolLabels-locale-parity-7481.test.ts

Read: card #34372 (body and all 8 comments), PR #38193 (body, 5 files, net diff against merge-base `7605e0c9`), the check-runs on this head. The changeset is judged in ② only.

### ① Derived judgments

- `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE['service-ai-studio']` gains `'list_flow_runs'`, between `get_record_history` and `list_metadata`. Sorted order holds. **Right.**
- `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES.has('list_flow_runs')` and `isPlatformProvidedToolName('list_flow_runs')` move from `false` to `true`. No export is added, removed or retyped; `api-surface/`, `authorable-surface/` and `authorable-defaults/` are untouched by the diff. **Right.**
- `validateAiToolReferences` (`packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts`, read, not in the diff) stops emitting the `ai-skill-tool-unresolved` finding for a skill naming `list_flow_runs`. That finding is `severity: 'warning'` at all four emit sites; `SkillSchema.tools` is a free string array and parsed this name before and after. So the widening is of the lint's resolution universe (a public surface), not of any schema accept set. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is **right**, as on #32668.
- MCP bridge (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`, read): `worldAnnotation` now answers `openWorldHint: false` for a bridged tool of this name. It gets no `readOnlyHint`, since `PLATFORM_READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES` is a curated five and omission is the conservative default; `get_record_history` is treated the same. **Right**; the changeset does not mention it, as no earlier registry row did.
- Chat labels: `chatbot.tool.list_flow_runs` is present in all 11 packs under `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/` on this head (landed by #34379), so the 7481 parity case over `COVERED` holds with the name now read from the registry. **Right.**
- Cherry-pick resolution: against `7605e0c9` the diff of the `hits` file is additive apart from one list-comma rewording (`, and the ask agent's ask_which` became `, the ask agent's ask_which`); main's `ask_which` sentence with `cloud#4773` and main's `get_record_context` spec case are both intact. `main` moved to `4f7aa88a` without touching any of the four source files. **Nothing lost.**

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — agreed.

M1 (must-fix) — the changeset grades `@objectstack/spec` **minor** under `Metadata-protocol: added`, and the diff does not earn it. AGENTS.md defines the kind as "the change to what a metadata author can write — a new key, accepted value or metadata type ... all else is `none`", and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` states "a `minor` is earned by a change to the metadata protocol and by nothing else". Here nothing an author can write changes: `skill.tools[]` accepted the string `list_flow_runs` before and after, no authorable-surface shard moves, and the only behavioural difference is one advisory lint warning that is no longer emitted. The two earlier rows in this same array were landed as `Metadata-protocol: none` with `@objectstack/spec` patch: `get_record_history` (#32668, `Clause-②: yes` / `none`) and `ask_which` (#37989). The card itself asks for patch (Expected, item 3). The `Check Changeset` run is green only because `added` beside a `minor` is self-consistent; the gate cannot see whether the kind is true ("the declaration, not the diff, is still the carrier"). Because the fixed group versions in lockstep, an unearned minor lifts every package. Fix: `Metadata-protocol: none` in the PR body and the changeset body, and the entry graded `patch`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)` stays. If the seat holds that a newly resolved tool name IS an `added` accepted value, that reverses two landed precedents and is the maintainer's ruling to make, not this PR's.

The changeset prose is otherwise accurate against the tree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in dev report 7235338658. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, three gates not measured locally (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run scripts/`): CI owns them. At read time the head had 0 failed check-runs; `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Live E2E UI` and the lint families concluded success; `Build Core`, `Test Core` 1-10, `Test UI` 1-16, `Build & E2E UI`, `Type Check · workspace` and `· consumer gates` were still in progress. Those conclusions are owed before any PASS on a later head; this record does not rest on them.
- Producer: the cloud repository is not readable from this seat, so "cloud `service-ai-studio` registers `list_flow_runs`" is taken from the card and from the 7481 file on `main` (its `AHEAD_OF_PIN` note, sourced from cloud `plugin.ts`), not read first-hand. The cloud conformance test is the owner of that fact (card item 4).
- SQL push-down: not applicable; the diff has no data access.

### ④ Design judgment

`platform-tool-names.ts` (hits): the row sits in the right group (the build agent's package), in order, and the jsdoc sentence agrees with the card's description and with the changeset. Every reader of the registry in the tree was read (lint universe, MCP world hint, 7481 parity, `check-i18n-call-site-keys` exemption, qa door-rules corpus prose): none enumerates the group in a way this row breaks. The group's own invariant, "the exact set that package registers", holds on the card's word (see ③).

`platform-tool-names.test.ts`: the pin and its control (`list_flow_run` misses) agree with the contract. `validate-ai-tool-references.test.ts`: the pin resolves the name and the control (`retry_flow_run` reported at `skills[0].tools[1]`) fails on an over-wide universe. Both agree.

`toolLabels-locale-parity-7481.test.ts`: `AHEAD_OF_PIN` empties and `GRADUATED` gains the name, which is what the file's own note prescribes; the `GRADUATED` guard makes the row's removal red.

- M1 (must-fix) — see ②.
- N1 (nit) — the jsdoc names no cloud reference for `list_flow_runs`, where every other late arrival in that sentence carries one (`cloud#3565`, `#3656`, `#4347`, `#4773`). Follow-up or accepted deviation.
- N2 (nit) — in the 7481 file, `zh: the other four newly-mapped tools resolve too` loops over `AHEAD_OF_PIN`, which this PR empties, so the case asserts nothing again; iterating `GRADUATED` would keep it live. Label presence in every pack is still held by the `it.each` case.
